title: Better AI Models Won't Fix Your Engineering Team — Nicholas Arcolano, Jellyfish
talk_summary: Jellyfish analyzed telemetry from ~50k engineers at 447 companies and found that model/tool choice explains <1% of variance in merged-PR throughput, while skill use (~3%), token consumption (~9%), company/team environment (~12%), and individual engineer (~75%) dominate. The core message is that leaders should invest in controllable factors—harness customization, consumption, review culture, and people—rather than chasing model upgrades.

takeaways.technique: Invest in reusable skills/harness customization over model swaps
takeaways.what_they_do: They measure 'skill use' (skills, cursor rules, harness customization) per engineer-week and find high skill use correlates with materially higher PR throughput, while model family changes show no statistical effect.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you get up to 30 plus runs uh of using skills uh per engineer per week, that's a 30% bump just from that factor alone
takeaways.numbers: ~30% PR throughput bump at 30+ skill runs/engineer/week; skill use explains ~3% of variance vs <1% for tool/model

takeaways.technique: Token consumption as the dominant controllable throughput lever with diminishing returns
takeaways.what_they_do: They plot token spend vs merged PRs per developer-week across 500k developer-weeks and find a saturating curve: more tokens yield more output, with top-decile users roughly doubling output at ~10x tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can basically double your output between the median and the top 10%. It costs you about 10x the tokens.
takeaways.numbers: 2x output for ~10x tokens (median to top decile); consumption explains ~9% of variance

takeaways.technique: Treat review process/culture as a first-class throughput factor
takeaways.what_they_do: They decompose the 'where you work' factor and find roughly one-third team, two-thirds company—codebase, review process, culture—with a 2x spread between top and bottom decile companies holding token consumption fixed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your culture, your team, your company, there's a lot of variation just in those things even for fixed AI spend
takeaways.numbers: 2x spread between top 10% and bottom 10% companies at fixed consumption; environment explains ~12% of variance

takeaways.technique: Fix idle agents by improving work supply and environment, not by adding models
takeaways.what_they_do: The talk's framing implies throughput variance is dominated by organizational factors (work availability, process, culture) rather than tooling; leaders should change the 'course' they control.
takeaways.evidence_quote: unlike golf, you can change the course. You can change your environment.

takeaways.technique: Use natural-experiment / A-B telemetry instead of vibes for tooling decisions
takeaways.what_they_do: They exploit an external shock (Cursor promoting Grok) as a natural experiment and compare each engineer's PR throughput to same-company peers, finding no correlation—an example of measuring tool changes against a controlled baseline.
takeaways.numbers: No statistically significant throughput change from forced model switch
